summary: Release 2 retains the validated startup optimizations and closes the executable FlashInfer XQA runtime contract discovered by the release 1 fleet canary.

supersedes.immutability_guard: Release 1, its manifest, and its derived image remain unchanged. Build and select a new release 2 image; never retag or mutate release 1 in place.

delivery.application_guard: Export the complete vllm Python package from source.code_commit. Do not copy only the changed files onto the v0.27.1 Python package.
delivery.configuration_guard: A profile/configuration run may select an existing image for this patch set, but must not build or modify it.
delivery.release_guard: The fleet must assign release 2 a new immutable image tag and digest. Release 1 must remain available only as failed-canary evidence, not as a deployment target.

components.reason: Move processor warmup off the serial engine-start critical path while retaining warmup behavior.
components.removal_condition: Remove after an equivalent upstream implementation is present in the pinned base.

components.reason: Expose queue depth, reader count, bounce-buffer size, copy-block size, and direct-I/O selection through model_loader_extra_config.
components.removal_condition: Remove after the installed vLLM and FastSafetensors releases expose equivalent validated controls.

components.reason: Avoid materializing non-local Qwen byte ranges and avoid duplicate MTP embedding and lm_head loads.
components.removal_condition: Remove after the Qwen implementations upstream provide equivalent filtering and weight sharing.

components.reason: Use aligned O_DIRECT reads for cold selected ranges and buffered reads for resident checkpoints.
components.removal_condition: Remove after the behavior is available in compatible released vLLM and FastSafetensors versions.

components.reason: Persist and reuse an exact KV allocation so redundant multimodal memory profiling can be skipped without disabling compilation, warmup, sampling, or CUDA graphs.
components.removal_condition: Remove after the pinned vLLM release persists the exact allocation with equivalent fingerprinting and invalidation.

dependencies.name: fastsafetensors
dependencies.reason: Provides bounded parallel no-GDS reads and adaptive aligned O_DIRECT support required by this patch set.

tested_runtime.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition

compatibility.source_rule: The Python source is pinned to source.code_commit, which is based on source.base_commit from upstream/main and is not the v0.27.1 release source tree.
compatibility.porting_rule: For a different vLLM source release, port the five commits, update this manifest, and repeat unit, startup, correctness, memory, and serving-performance gates before deployment.

mounts.reason: FlashInfer XQA requires either compatible precompiled cubins or a CUDA compiler. This release uses the production host toolkit for JIT compilation.
Persist vLLM, Torch, startup-plan, and FlashInfer JIT artifacts across container removal and model switches.

runtime_requirements.runtime_guard: Apply the activation environment before importing vLLM or FlashInfer. Run the preflight inside the candidate image with these production mounts, not against the unmounted image filesystem.

preflight.execution_context: Inside the candidate container with the production mounts and activation environment applied
argv: import shutil; from vllm.utils.flashinfer import has_flashinfer; assert shutil.which('nvcc') == '/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc'; assert has_flashinfer()
preflight.reason: Release 1 imported flashinfer-python but had neither flashinfer-cubin nor nvcc on PATH, so vLLM selected XQA and then rejected the backend during CUDA-graph memory profiling.

release_1_canary.failure: FlashInfer selected decode_backend=xqa, but vLLM reported that the FlashInfer backend was unavailable because the mounted nvcc executable was absent from PATH.

release_2_local_preflight.evidence: With the production CUDA mount and /usr/local/cuda/bin added to PATH, shutil.which('nvcc') resolved to /usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc and vllm.utils.flashinfer.has_flashinfer() returned true.

requirements: The engine completes profile_cudagraph_memory and CUDA-graph setup without a FlashInfer backend error.
The configured API readiness endpoint succeeds.
The service and container restart counters remain zero from launch through readiness and the representative serving check.
A successful first start and representative MTP request populate a non-empty /var/cache/vllm/.cache/flashinfer tree on the persistent cache mount.
Record the FlashInfer cache artifact paths after the first successful run, then remove and recreate the container with the same cache mount.
The second start reaches API readiness with decode_backend=xqa and zero restarts without rebuilding the already-recorded XQA artifacts.
The previously recorded FlashInfer cache artifacts remain present and are reused from the persistent mount.

remaining_gates: Run a fixed correctness request and representative MTP depth-5 generation after API readiness.
Run representative TTFT, ITL, throughput, and peak host RAM/VRAM checks on the final release 2 image.
Verify rollback to the stock image and profile without selecting release 1.

excluded_experiments.reason: Below the agreed materiality threshold and adds cache invalidation surface.
Constructor-only gain with no stable end-to-end win.
Below the agreed materiality threshold and model-specific maintenance cost.

external_fleet_requirements: Keep the shared-role FlashInfer 0.6.16 Python 3.11 shim that inserts 'from __future__ import annotations' in fd_exchange.py.
Keep the shared-role dependency pins fastapi==0.136.3, starlette==0.52.1, and prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator==7.1.0.
Inject Hugging Face credentials through the fleet secret mechanism; do not place tokens in the image, manifest, profile, or service unit.

rollback.method: Select the prior stock image and remove the patch-set-specific FastSafetensors configuration, activation environment, and startup-plan opt-in. Do not fall back to release 1.
rollback.data: The startup-plan and FlashInfer workspace directories are regenerable cache data and may remain on disk; incompatible fingerprints, schemas, or compiled artifacts must not be treated as release identity.
